newsitem.title: PERU: Peru to scrap Cenbank March CD auctions - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Peru to scrap Cenbank March CD auctions - dealers.

text.p: Peru's Central Bank will continue to refrain in March from holding its twice-weekly auction of certificates of deposit (CD) due to tight liquidity in the financial system since mid-January, dealers said.
Dealers said the lack of liquidity in the market will worsen in the second and third weeks of March as companies sell dollars to buy soles to pay income and sales taxes.
Liquidity also will depend on 1996 company profits, which are due to be announced in March, and on corporate tax payments.
No Central Bank spokesman would comment on the reports.
The last Central Bank auction was held on Jan. 15, when the bank placed 20 million soles worth of 56-day CDs at an average annual interest rate of 15.45 percent.
In five CD auctions so far this year, the bank has placed a total of 224 million soles worth of CDs.
"The bank will return to the market to auction CDs when interest rates diminish as a result of improved liquidity," a trader from a leading local bank said.
The Central Bank auctions CDs to sop up excess liquidity and prevent the sol falling against the dollar.
